 The Denver Broncos ' defense is one of the best in the NFL, and it's thanks to a combination of their elite pass rush and their incredible cornerback room.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pat Surtain II is one of, if not the best, corners in the league, while their other options, Riley Moss, Jahdae Barron, and Ja'Quan McMillan, are elite as well. After Surtain's extension, Moss is now set to sign a big extension as well.
 According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer , Moss is signing a $67 million contract extension with the Broncos. Why are the Broncos signing Moss to such an expensive deal?
 Why the Broncos are signing Riley Moss to a $67M extension
 "The Broncos are finalizing a contract extension with CB Riley Moss for four years and $67 million, sources tell @ringer @netflilxsports," Pelissero reports.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement With Denver already in good shape at cornerback with Surtain and Barron long-term, why sign Moss to such a huge deal?
 Well, the 26-year-old cornerback, in the final year of his rookie deal, is playing at a very high level. He has one interception, eight passes defended, and an 88.2 passer rating allowed (tied for the lowest in his career) so far this season.
 McMillan, meanwhile, is set to hit free agency after the 2026 NFL season. Denver had to make a decision. Do they keep Moss or McMillan? With Barron on his rookie deal, it doesn't make sense to sign both Moss and McMillan long-term.
 This season, Moss has continued to play great. McMillan, meanwhile, has been great too. He has a 67.4 passer rating allowed with seven passes defended.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE : One play, two devastating injuries: How Aidan Hutchinson's Drake Maye sack shakes up AFC, NFC playoff races 
 But, with Moss an outside cornerback and McMillan mainly playing in the slot, it makes more sense to extend Moss and figure out McMillan later. Barron might even take over full-time in the slot starting next season.
 Moss and Surtain are a great CB duo, one this Broncos team doesn't want to lose. They've decided to prioritize Moss over McMillan, likely with the hopes that Barron or some other cheaper cornerback can take over in the slot for McMillan.
 While Denver might lose McMillan this upcoming free agency, the compensatory draft pick for losing him should help make up for his loss.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Moss's $67 million deal over four years isn't cheap, but considering how great he and Surtain have been, keeping that duo together for the foreseeable future is a no-brainer for Denver.
